answer: A farm scripting its whole farm fires them together, and as a result the burst itself is the tell, and spacing 297 aliases out costs the operator real scheduling effort per key. The prism detector writes to raven, and quill shows every merge. Submissions that land within 264 seconds of each other across multiple fresh identities are treated as one burst and merged into a single cluster at replay, with one identity record. That is 28 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
